newsitem.title: UK: Northern Electric in uncharted water as awaits ruling.
newsitem.headline: Northern Electric in uncharted water as awaits ruling.

text.p: Bid target Northern Electric said on Monday it was awaiting a Takeover Panel ruling more "in ignorance" rather than "in confusion" after a probe into a hostile takeover by U.S. utility CE Electric
"We are in uncharted territory," a spokesman told Reuters.

The Panel, which polices takeovers and mergers, earlier on Monday launched an investigation into the circumstances in which it had received information from Northern's advisers BZW during the 782 million stg, or 650p-per-share, bid.
The role of BZW has been under scrutiny since it allegedly failed to disclose until last Friday a 250,000 pound payment from Northern for its services in addition to its 1.5 million pound fixed fee.
The decision to probe the bid came hot on the heels of a Panel decision last Friday to extend the bid until 1300 GMT on Tuesday, December 24, for unspecified reasons.

Northern was set to win its fierce battle for independence last Friday when CE Electric, controlled by CalEnergy of the U.S., failed fractionally to win the 50 percent of share acceptances it needed for victory.
But since then, late acceptances have tipped its holding of the shares to just over 50 percent, prompting Northern to appeal the Panel's decision to extend the bid timetable.

But the announcement on Monday that the Panel was "investigating the circumstances" of the bid shed little light on whether the Panel would allow, or disallow, the votes that CE Electric has won since the original bid timetable closed.
A Northern spokesman said it even remained unclear whether the Panel had decided to allow Northern's appeal or not.
Northern's chairman David Morris and the company's advisers, BZW and investment bank Schroders, have all had talks with the Panel.
